subject.title: Long streaming model responses cause event loop starvation

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a core runtime fairness fix for long model streams now, and should the boundary be cooperative yielding, worker/off-thread stream processing, or lane preemption coordinated with the broader starvation issues?
rationale: The reported bug is credible, but the current code already contains partial mitigations and the remaining fix shape affects core Gateway/agent architecture rather than a narrow known line-level repair.

options.title: Require current-main stress proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a fresh long-output Gateway proof before authorizing a specific implementation path.

options.title: Sponsor a core fairness fix now
options.body: Treat this as a P1 core stability project and choose the runtime boundary for yielding, off-thread processing, or lane preemption up front.

options.title: Fold into lane-starvation umbrella
options.body: Move the remaining decision to a broader canonical lane-fairness issue if maintainers want one product direction for model_call starvation, preemption, and operator recovery.

recommendation.title: Require current-main stress proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a fresh long-output Gateway proof before authorizing a specific implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct current-main history connects this owner to the OpenAI-compatible stream mitigation and adjacent Gateway runtime performance work.
